Summary: Creeping things that creep upon the earth — worms, snails, moles, and the like — are unclean and may not be eaten.
Commandment: Do not eat any creeping thing that creeps upon the earth.
Application: The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. The creeping kinds were wholly excluded from Israel's table. The New Testament records these food distinctions set aside (Mark 7:19; Acts 10).
Purpose: To mark Israel's table as distinct (Leviticus 11). The New Testament records the distinctions set aside: Jesus declares all foods clean (Mark 7:19) and Peter's vision confirms it (Acts 10).
